g.text: The Four Ontology Hierarchies in Detail
Each ontology is a structured node hierarchy. The hierarchies are how custodians articulate intent in a form the agents can read.
The why: who uses the system, what outcomes they need, which scenarios drive each outcome
The how it looks and behaves: from the user journey down to the atomic design tokens
The where: services, integration boundaries, infrastructure layers, dependency map
The what the code actually does: ﬁle structure down to statements, plus boundary endpoints
Structural hierarchies that the ingestion agents extract from the live system and that the custodians curate as the system evolves.
